# @spellkave/gateway-identity

> `authkit-refresh-token` — Identity, auth, rate-limit and world-catalog helpers for the gateway services, and `authkit-refresh-token`, which mints a simulated player's AuthKit access token (ADR-0124 D-7).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `authkit-refresh-token [player]` | Spend the player's refresh token at AuthKit, keep the rotated one in the runtime file, print the access token (stdout holds only the token, so `> file` is safe). `player` defaults to `$SPELLKAVE_SIM_NAME`, then `sim1`; `SPELLKAVE_MACHINE_SEED_FILE` and `SPELLKAVE_MACHINE_RUNTIME_FILE` replace the default paths. A missing seed is installed with `scripts/sim/install-machine-seed.sh --player <name>`. |

Exit codes: `0` the access token is on stdout; `1` refused, one `authkit-refresh-token: <reason>` line on stderr. Operators run it through `scripts/sim/authkit-refresh-token.sh` (token cache, per-player lock).

How it answers and fails, with real records, is in [the guide](docs/guide.md#how-it-answers).

What `authkit-refresh-token` does is described and tested from the outside: 3 scenarios in [`behaviour/`](behaviour/) drive the real tool. The last run produced [`docs/guide.md`](docs/guide.md) (short, for people and agents) and [`docs/scenarios.md`](docs/scenarios.md) (every scenario with its transcripts).

## Design

Each part's header comment, as written next to the code.

### [`src/bin/authkit-refresh-token.ts`](src/bin/authkit-refresh-token.ts)

Print one AuthKit access token for the loop machine user (stdout only).
Seed comes from a provisioned machine-user.seed.json; the rotated
refresh token is written only to the host runtime file (ADR-0124 D-7).

### [`src/refresh-auth.ts`](src/refresh-auth.ts)

Headless AuthKit refresh-token grant for the improvement-loop machine user
(ADR-0124 D-7 / sk-t2qm.11.6 option A).

Hits `{issuer}/oauth2/token` — the same AuthKit-domain Connect endpoint
the website uses — with RFC 8707 `resource=https://mcp.spellkave.com/mcp`
so `iss`/`aud`/`sub` match an interactive login. Never calls
`POST /user_management/authenticate`.

Provisioning supplies the seed (non-rotating identifiers + initial refresh_token).
AuthKit rotates the refresh token on every use, so the live token is
written only to a host-side runtime file (separate from the seed and from
the ReadOnly gateway container).

The loop owns this exchange. The Account API never sees the refresh token.

### [`src/world-identity.ts`](src/world-identity.ts)

SpacetimeDB world identity preimage (ADR-0102 D-2).
Identity = BLAKE3(iss|sub) from the access token handed to withToken().
Same iss+sub ⇒ same world identity; a different iss is a different person.

## Behaviour suite

From [`vitest.behaviour.config.ts`](vitest.behaviour.config.ts):

Behaviour suite: behaviour/*.feature drive the real authkit-refresh-token
binary against a fake HTTPS AuthKit, each scenario in its own temp HOME.
Needs the openssl CLI and the repository's tsx; no node, no outside network.
`pnpm guide` turns the last run into docs/guide.md and docs/scenarios.md.

From [`behaviour/steps.ts`](behaviour/steps.ts):

The sentences of behaviour/*.feature, against the real
src/bin/authkit-refresh-token.ts run through the repository's tsx, as
scripts/sim/authkit-refresh-token.sh runs it; nothing under src/ is imported.
Each scenario gets a temp HOME (so ~/.config/spellkave/... lands there) and
its own fake AuthKit (support/fake-authkit.ts), so scenarios share nothing.

From [`behaviour/support/fake-authkit.ts`](behaviour/support/fake-authkit.ts):

A fake AuthKit token endpoint for behaviour scenarios: an HTTPS server on an
ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port that records every request and answers with what
the scenario set. A tool under test never reaches the real AuthKit.

Why HTTPS: the machine-user refresh grant (ADR-0124 D-7) refuses any issuer
that is not an `https://` AuthKit domain, and it derives the token endpoint
from the issuer. So the fake gets a self-signed certificate (made once per
process with `openssl`), and the child process trusts it through
`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, a standard Node variable. The tool needs no test-only
URL override and runs exactly as in production.

Answers follow the OAuth 2.0 token-endpoint shapes (RFC 6749 §5.1 success,
§5.2 error), which AuthKit's `/oauth2/token` uses. Nothing here imports the
package's `src/`, so other suites (a gateway, a CLI) can reuse it as is.

## Unit tests

A unit test stays only for what the behaviour suite cannot reach. The line above each test says why (`// keep(K…): …`, or one `// keep-file(K…): …` line for a whole file), or names the scenario it still lacks (`// open: …`).

- **K1** one of several cases over a pure function
- **K2** a branch the public surface cannot provoke without an injected host, process, fault or TTY
- **K3** a cross-run invariant (determinism, idempotence, ordering)
- **K4** a compile proof, snapshot or documentation drift gate
- **K5** a contract with another tool the suite does not drive (shell scripts, shared file formats)
